name: Glute kickback
angleNote: Hip flexion: positive = thigh in front of the body (start), negative = behind (end). Lifting makes the angle smaller. Hip at the origin.

segments.massNote: Segment mass as a fraction of body mass, and centre of mass as a fraction of the segment length from its proximal end. Approximate textbook anthropometry. The lower leg includes the foot.
segments.massSource: TODO: check against a published anthropometric table (e.g. Dempster's segment parameters as tabulated by Winter)
segments.note: Hip→knee and knee→ankle in metres, typical adult.

strengthCurve.label: Hip extensor strength
strengthCurve.note: Relative hip-extension torque, assumed strongest with the hip bent and weakest behind the body. Approximate shape.
strengthCurve.source: TODO: verify against published torque–angle data

muscles.name: Gluteus maximus
muscles.note: Main hip extensor, working hardest near full hip extension.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.note: Help extend the hip, more so when it is bent. With the knee bent (kneeling) they are shorter and help less, which these weights ignore.

muscles.name: Adductor magnus
muscles.note: Its rear part is a strong hip extensor when the hip is bent.

phases.name: End
phases.text: Thigh behind the body: glutes at their shortest.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: Standing at a cable this is the start; on hands and knees the thigh passes through here.

phases.name: Hip bent
phases.text: Only the kneeling version starts this deep.

variants.name: Standing cable kickback
variants.notes: Standing on the other leg, cable from a low pulley in front. Use the range from about 30° to −25°; the cable pulls the leg forward all the way, and the leg's own weight helps on the way back.

variants.name: Kneeling kickback (ankle weight)
variants.notes: On hands and knees with the knee bent 90°. Lifting the bent leg works against the leg's own weight too; torque peaks around 45°, when the whole leg is furthest from the hip horizontally.

variants.name: Standing glute kickback machine

camProfile.note: Effective radius in metres: joint torque per unit of stack weight, including any lever or pulley ratio. Illustrative shape, not measured from a specific machine.
